airport.name: Esquel Brigadier Antonio Parodi International Airport

summary: Esquel Brigadier Antonio Parodi International Airport serves the Patagonian town of Esquel in Chubut Province, Argentina, acting as the main air gateway to the Andean region of northwest Patagonia. Named after Argentine Air Force Brigadier Antonio Parodi, the airport provides access to Los Alerces National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the famous La Hoya ski resort. Its location at the foot of the Andes makes it a popular arrival point for adventure travelers heading into the Patagonian wilderness.
faqs:
Q: How far is the airport from Esquel city center?
A: The airport is located approximately 15 km (about 9 miles) east of downtown Esquel, with a typical drive taking around 20 minutes.

Q: Are there regular commercial flights to Esquel?
A: Yes, the airport receives regular flights primarily from Buenos Aires operated by Aerolineas Argentinas and LADE, though schedules can be seasonal and weather-dependent.

Q: What is Esquel best known for visiting?
A: Esquel is the main gateway to Los Alerces National Park, known for its ancient alerce trees, glacial lakes, and hiking trails, as well as the La Trochita historic narrow-gauge railway and La Hoya ski resort.

Q: Is the airport affected by weather?
A: Flights can be disrupted by strong Patagonian winds and winter snowfall, so travelers should allow flexibility in their plans, especially during the winter months.
transport_tips: Remises (private hire cars) and taxis are available outside the terminal and are the most reliable way to reach Esquel town. Rental car agencies operate at the airport and are recommended for those planning to explore Los Alerces National Park or surrounding areas independently. There is no public bus service directly connecting the airport to the city, so arranging ground transport in advance is advisable.
local_tip: Pack layers and windproof clothing year-round—Esquel's location at the foot of the Andes means weather can shift rapidly, and the Patagonian wind makes even mild temperatures feel significantly colder, especially on early morning flights.
